Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been working these 10.1 mu for twenty years now, so I have a pretty clear routine — I don't need to reinvent things every season. My ground is split like this: about 7.1 mu on the better plots for the wheat-maize rotation, and about 3 mu on the sandier piece for cotton. That split has worked for us and I'm not changing it this year.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October).** I planted about 7.1 mu of wheat back in early October, like I always do — the ground was still warm and moisture was OK. Used "Jimai 22" seed, same variety as the last few years because it's been steady. Before planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (the 15-15-15 kind from the agri store) as base fertilizer, worked it in with the rotary tiller. I gave it the winter water in December to settle it in. Now in spring, once it greens up and starts jointing, I'll topdress about 12 kg of urea per mu and irrigate at the same time — that's the most important water of the year. If it's a dry spring I'll give it one more irrigation at heading. The extension person a few years back told us to split nitrogen more — apply less at base and more at topdress — and I've been doing that since, it does seem to help. Last year I got about 430 kg/mu on these plots, so I'm expecting something similar unless weather turns bad. I'll spray herbicide once in early spring for the weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I'll do one insecticide pass.

**Maize (planting in mid-June).** Right after wheat harvest in early June I'll plant summer maize on the same ground — no-till direct seeding, because there's only about a week between harvest and planting and I can't afford to lose days. I hire a neighbor with a no-till planter, costs about 30 yuan/mu but saves me a lot of trouble. I'll use "Zhengdan 958" or whatever hybrid seed the store has that's similar — it yields well here. I apply a starter compound fertilizer with the planter, about 30 kg/mu. Then at the big trumpet stage (about 50-60 days in) I topdress 15 kg of urea per mu and irrigate if it hasn't rained. Usually in summer we get enough rain, so I only irrigate once or twice for maize. Last year maize was around 500 kg/mu. Spray once for corn borer if I see damage.

**Cotton (planting late April).** On my 3 mu cotton plot I plant around April 20-25, using film mulch like everyone does here — the film costs something but it gives me an earlier start and holds moisture. I'll use a conventional cotton variety, nothing fancy. Cotton takes more fertilizer and more care than the grain crops. I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and I'll topdress urea (about 10 kg/mu) at the budding stage and again at flowering if the plants look like they need it. Cotton needs 2 irrigations usually — once at budding and once at boll-setting. The pests are the hard part — I'll spray for aphids, spider mites, and bollworm probably 4-5 times across the season. That's where most of the pesticide cost goes. Picking cotton is the hardest work — my two daughters-in-law help when they're home, and my husband and I do the rest. We pick 3-4 times through September and October. If lint comes out around 260-280 kg/mu I'll be happy.

**On labor and cash.** Two of my sons work off-farm so I can't count on them for planting or harvest. I manage most field operations myself with help from my husband and the daughters-in-law when they're around. I hire the combine for wheat and maize harvest and the no-till planter — about 60-70 yuan/mu for combine, 30 for planting. It's worth it, my back can't do what it used to. For cotton picking I rely on family only — hiring pickers is too expensive for 3 mu.

I'm not planning any big changes this year. Fertilizer prices haven't dropped so I'll stick with what I did last year. If I see the wheat looking especially strong at jointing I might add a few extra kg of urea, but otherwise I go with what I know.
